account:
Today there seems to be unusual activity around grain and bread supplies, but I do not yet know its purpose or scale. The secretary reported overhearing the builder discuss a grain shortage, seek the miller's help, and mention forty-six hay bales. That number is unverified. The neighbour said she saw the baker give bread to the innkeeper yesterday; the innkeeper was asking about spare wheat or hay, and freight was seeking the miller about arrangements. She also reported that the baker considered yesterday's bread arrangements successful and was baking fresh bread today. These reports suggest efforts to arrange food supplies, though I cannot establish whether there is an actual shortage or who needs the grain.

I attended my ten o'clock mill inspection but could not locate the miller, including after calling out. I also checked near the bakery without finding the baker then. Townsfolk repeated vague reports about a 'bridge or port change' at the bakery and the baker carrying a sack of bread. Their wording gives me no clear evidence of an actual transport change. I should not treat it as confirmed.

I am now back at the office for thirteen-hundred council letters and have asked the secretary for correspondence, while reporting that the grain stocks remain unverified. The baker has just come into view, walking near the great hall and holding an emerald; I do not know why he is here. Later I have tea with the neighbour at fifteen hundred, office business at sixteen-thirty, and the confirmed eighteen-hundred great-hall lighting inspection with the builder. The builder arranged to meet me shortly beforehand and accompany me inside. That appointment appears to be ordinary town business; I have seen nothing establishing a connection between the lighting inspection and the supply discussions.
